issues.body:
## Problem

The v2 migration iterates graph nodes with for...of even though production nodes are keyed objects. An affected legacy chat can throw before reaching the v5 rebuild gate. Edge embeddings are omitted; existing tests use array-shaped nodes.

## Evidence

- `src/store/migrations/v2.js — migrateEmbeddings`
- `src/store/schemas.js — GraphDataSchema`
- `tests/store/migrations.test.js — legacy embedding fixture`

## Proposed fix

1. Iterate keyed graph collections with Object.values; support historically valid array fixtures only if needed for compatibility.
2. Convert legacy embeddings for memories, nodes, edges, and the actual legacy community fields without overwriting valid Base64 data.
3. Keep the sequential migration and rollback behavior; do not bypass mandatory v5 rebuild gating.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A production-shaped v1 graph reaches the current migration result without throwing.
- [ ] All supported legacy embedding fields convert once; existing Base64, absent collections, and repeat runs are safe.
- [ ] Regression fixtures include keyed nodes, edges, partial conversion, and migration rollback.

## Priority and scope

P1 — address first: correctness/data safety or the architecture contract that protects it. This issue proposes work; it does not claim the fix is implemented.

issues.body:
## Problem

Entity rename deletes old edge hashes without queuing rewritten edges for sync, and entity deletion removes connected edges without deleting their vectors. Text replacement paths also need consistent deletion of the old indexed text.

## Evidence

- `src/store/chat-data.js — updateEntity, deleteEntity, updateMemory, mergeEntities`
- `src/graph/graph.js — syncNode and edge text/hash construction`
- `src/store/AGENTS.md — stChanges contract`

## Proposed fix

1. Centralize exact indexed-text construction and replacement changesets: delete the previous hash when synced, invalidate stale embedding/sync state, and queue the new text.
2. For rename, update node and connected edge IDs/text; for deletion, include every connected synced edge.
3. Audit memory-summary and entity-description updates against the same contract; keep network I/O in orchestrators.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Synced rename emits exact old node/edge hashes and replacement sync items.
- [ ] Deletion removes the node and connected edge vectors; unsynced items do not produce phantom deletes.
- [ ] Text updates replace indexed content without leaving the old vector; hash payloads remain numeric.
- [ ] Behavioral tests cover synced/unsynced edits, rename collisions, deletion, and unchanged text.

## Problem

Converted guidance preserves the old dynamic-RAG description. It omits archive/rebuild invariants, gives a broader impression of POV enforcement than the archive implements, and links schema sources that still say v4 or v3.

## Evidence

## Proposed fix

1. Adopt the world/story-memory-first direction of #3: immutable narrative history, dynamic POV-aware recall, and evolving current-world state.
2. Document durable chat metadata versus settings/runtime caches/optional derived vector indexes; preserve local-first execution and provider-independent structured outputs.

- [ ] All non-ready lifecycle states and archive safety checkpoints have explicit guidance and implementation pointers.

issues.body:
## Problem

The store guide requires expectedChatId, but migration/event saves and several store mutators still use unguarded save calls. Multi-step operations that yield need a consistent way to avoid acting on a newly selected chat.

- `src/store/chat-data.js — saveOpenVaultData and mutation save call sites`
- `src/store/migrations/AGENTS.md — rollback example`

## Proposed fix

1. Trace each multi-step mutation and capture chat identity before its first asynchronous boundary.
2. Route saves through the guarded repository API and recheck identity/session cancellation before subsequent state updates or network synchronization.
3. Handle guard failure as cancellation without mutating the newly selected chat or performing a stale rollback.
4. Update the rollback example to use the dependency boundary and captured chat ID. Do not claim every immediate synchronous save is already a reproduced race.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Deferred-save tests switch chats at meaningful await boundaries and show no new-chat mutation or stale follow-up sync.
- [ ] Unchanged-chat edits and migrations persist successfully.
- [ ] Migration failure restores only the originating chat snapshot and retains session-scoped failure handling.

issues.body:
## Problem

The accumulator is reset before generation and the catch path only logs. The guide promises restoration, while the implementation comments intentionally consume it to avoid repeated calls. The retry policy must be made explicit.

## Evidence

- `src/extraction/extract.js — synthesizeReflections accumulator reset/catch`
- `src/reflection/AGENTS.md — failure restoration claim`
- `src/state.js — session lifecycle`

## Proposed fix

1. Proposed policy: snapshot the consumed amount and restore it on failure or cancellation only to the originating chat/character, preserving importance added meanwhile.
2. Prevent immediate retries with a per-character bounded retry/cooldown marker scoped to the session; centralize thresholds and clear markers on chat reset.
3. Define how a successful empty/deduplicated response consumes the trigger; do not retry it as a transport failure.
4. Document the chosen policy and avoid charging another LLM call on every worker wake.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Success consumes the intended amount; failure preserves it without overwriting newly accumulated importance.
- [ ] Repeated failures cannot create an uncontrolled retry loop.

## Problem

New rebuild/archive code reads raw extension settings and repeats fallback values; CDN/queue infrastructure logs directly despite the documented dependency/settings/logger boundaries.

## Evidence

- `src/rebuild/rebuild.js — raw getExtensionSettings`
- `src/archive/archive.js — settings entry points and fallback thresholds`
- `src/utils/cdn.js; src/utils/queue.js — direct console calls`
- `src/settings.js; src/constants.js; src/utils/logging.js`

## Proposed fix

1. Route runtime settings reads through getSettings; keep pure functions receiving explicit settings snapshots and source defaults from constants.
2. Move shared thresholds/protocol enums to central frozen definitions where appropriate; avoid turning every local implementation string into a global enum.
3. Route queue logging through injected loggers. For CDN bootstrap, choose a cycle-safe minimal logger/injected callback or document a narrow bootstrap exception supported by the import graph.
4. Update utils/root instructions to distinguish justified bootstrap boundaries from accidental bypasses.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Logger dependencies do not create a CDN/settings import cycle; injected test logging works.
- [ ] Warnings/errors remain visible and debug logging follows the intended toggle.
- [ ] Focused settings/cancellation checks preserve behavior; no unrelated architectural rewrite.

## Problem

Some fire-and-forget side-panel imports lack catches, Escape does not stop propagation as documented, and the guide names an obsolete World tab and the wrong settings initializer. Merge options carry unused data-key attributes that the rule forbids.

## Evidence

- `src/ui/render.js — side-panel imports and initBrowser`
- `src/ui/settings.js — modal Escape and bindUIElements`
- `src/ui/templates.js — merge datalist options`
- `templates/settings_panel.html; src/ui/AGENTS.md`

## Proposed fix

1. Catch fire-and-forget import failures with suitable reporting; avoid silent unhandled rejections.
2. Stop modal Escape propagation when OpenVault handles cancellation, preserving focus restoration and normal outside-modal behavior.
3. Remove unused option data-key attributes and keep text-based target resolution.
4. Describe the current six tabs and separate settings binding in bindUIElements from browser delegation in initBrowser; retain payload/reset invariants.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Escape cancels the OpenVault modal without reaching conflicting ST handlers; focus returns appropriately.

- [ ] Guide matches current tabs and initializer ownership; targeted interaction checks cover the changed behavior.

issues.body:
## Problem

The no-internal-mock rule and 3–5 orchestrator-test cap do not describe the existing suite, and literal prompt snapshots/real waits remain. More importantly, green tests missed production-shaped migration and ST community wiring.

## Evidence

- `tests/AGENTS.md; tests/setup.js`
- `tests/store/migrations.test.js; tests/retrieval/retrieve.test.js`
- `tests/graph/graph.test.js; tests/graph/communities.test.js`
- `tests/prompts; tests/extraction/fallback.test.js; tests/llm/llm.test.js`

## Proposed fix

1. Retain pure tests for pure logic and injected external boundaries for orchestration; replace the hard cap/locked-file language with a requirement that each integration test cover a distinct boundary or failure invariant.
2. Document narrow justified internal-mock exceptions without normalizing broad mocking of the behavior under test.
3. Replace brittle prose assertions with structural/behavioral protocol checks; retain stable required tokens only where semantically necessary.
4. Replace real timer waits in touched tests with fake timers or controlled deferred promises.
5. Use production-shaped factories and ensure regression tests in the linked fixes exercise real migration and retrieval composition. Avoid an indiscriminate suite rewrite.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Guidance permits necessary archive/rebuild/race regressions and states concrete mocking boundaries.
- [ ] No test required by the linked fixes is blocked by an arbitrary file count.
- [ ] Affected prompt/timer tests verify behavior without arbitrary prose snapshots or wall-clock sleeps.
- [ ] The migration-shape and ST orchestration regressions are covered in their respective fixes.
